subject.title: Import Scrollmark and twitter-web-exporter captures into the canonical local store

question: Should Birdclaw make Scrollmark canonical bundle v1 a supported core import contract, and what provenance, account-binding, completeness, and backup guarantees must that contract preserve?
rationale: The code can reuse existing import infrastructure, but source identity and semantic ownership become durable user-facing data contracts that cannot be selected safely from implementation details alone.

options.title: Approve canonical v1 first
options.body: Support only validated Scrollmark canonical bundle v1 initially, with explicit provenance and conservative collection-edge creation, while deferring legacy formats.

options.title: Approve all proposed formats
options.body: Support canonical bundles plus legacy Scrollmark and twitter-web-exporter shapes, accepting a larger compatibility and fixture-maintenance surface.

options.title: Keep external for now
options.body: Require a separate converter to emit Birdclaw’s supported backup/archive-compatible representation until the external schemas mature further.

recommendation.title: Approve canonical v1 first
recommendation.body: Support only validated Scrollmark canonical bundle v1 initially, with explicit provenance and conservative collection-edge creation, while deferring legacy formats.

likelyOwner.reason: The repository owner introduced and continues to maintain the archive/import architecture and is best positioned to approve a permanent source contract.
